predecessors.note: The page infobox: Preceded by the Gupta Empire; "The rise of the Mathara dynasty was probably linked to Samudragupta's forces having withdrawn from the region" (no date). Cliopatria draws this whole land as Gupta from 347 (149 of 149 cells) to 450 and 68 cells to 520.

successors.note: The page infobox: Succeeded by the Pitrbhakta dynasty and the Vasishtha dynasty; Umavarman, the Pitrbhakta king, overthrew Anantashaktivarman (undated). No dossier for either yet.
"Pishtapura then came under the Vasishtha dynasty. The Vasistha king Anantavarman issued an inscription from this city" (page, undated). No dossier yet.

capitals.name: Simhapura
capitals.note: Infobox capital Simhapura (Prabhanjanavarman's inscription was issued from it, and the Pitrbhakta Umavarman and his officer Matṛvara are at Simhapura later); the coordinates are approximate (the page gives none).

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe; Cliopatria has no Mathara row. The page: territory "mainly confined between the southern part of Odisha and the river Godavari", grants in Srikakulam district; Shaktivarman's copper-plate was issued at Pishtapura; the claim to rule to the Krishna or the Mahanadi is called an exaggeration. Cliopatria draws this land as Gupta (149 of 149 cells, 350-450; 68 cells 490-520), so this dossier contradicts the Gupta shape from the start.

region.text: Kalinga, "mainly confined between the southern part of Odisha and the river Godavari": the Srikakulam country (grants at Ragolu and Andhavaram), Pishtapura (Pithapuram) and Ganjam

ledger.note: c. 350: the Mathara dynasty rises in Kalinga. The page: the dynasty "ruled Kalinga from the mid-4th century to the end of the 5th century"; infobox "Established: c. 4th century CE"; Shaktivarman is the earliest known ruler, with the title Kalingadhipati and a copper-plate in his 13th regnal year from Pishtapura. The Gupta counterpart is the infobox's and Cliopatria's, not a dated event.

region.text: Kalinga, "mainly confined between the southern part of Odisha and the river Godavari": the Srikakulam country (grants at Ragolu and Andhavaram), Pishtapura (Pithapuram) and Ganjam

ledger.note: c. 499: the Mathara dynasty ends. "Anantashaktivarman appears to have been overthrown by the Pitrbhakta king Umavarman" (undated); the dynasty ruled "to the end of the 5th century" and "Disestablished: c. 5th century CE" in the infobox. The Matharas "fought the Vasisthas and the Pitrbhaktas for control of Kalinga" (undated).

wars.name: Mathara wars with the Vasishthas and Pitrbhaktas
wars.outcome: The Matharas fought the Vasishthas and the Pitrbhaktas for control of Kalinga; Umavarman of the Pitrbhaktas overthrew Anantashaktivarman and Pishtapura passed to the Vasishthas.
wars.note: The page gives no year for any of these fights; the years are the dynasty's span. The Mathara-Vishnukundin relation is not described (the Godavari-Krishna land was "controlled by the Shalankayanas and then the Vishnukundinas" in the 5th-6th centuries).

certainty.note: No border is given; the extent is the Kalinga coast between southern Odisha and the Godavari, with the Krishna claim called an exaggeration.

notes: New state Cliopatria lacks. One page opened (budget 2-5). All dates are the page's "mid-4th century to the end of the 5th century" (no ruler has an absolute date; only regnal years of single grants: Shaktivarman 13, Anantashaktivarman 14 and 28). Cliopatria draws the whole Mathara land as Gupta from 347 (Allahabad Pillar sphere); the gupta-empire dossier (sa-02-d) should record a loss here from c. 350 if the Mathara page is followed. Successors pitrbhakta-dynasty and vasishtha-dynasty have no dossier yet. Gazetteer names needed: Kalinga (the Odisha region has the alias), Simhapura, Pishtapura (Pithapuram).
